title: AI Daily Briefing
description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, open and local models, and AI in defense.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 23–30. New: OpenAI published an updated Model Spec on Oct. 29, and Tom's Hardware the same day reported figures from Anthropic's S-1 on where first-half compute spending went. The Oct. 23 offline-training item was removed to stay within the section count. No separate Google or Nvidia product announcement dated Oct. 29–30 was found. OpenAI's Oct. 29 post on frontier-model misalignment monitors was not carried because the OpenAI subsection was already at four items.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude is in six drug programs, and it acquired Mithril Medicine
items.summary: Anthropic said Oct. 27 that its life sciences team has research partnerships with BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group, and that it has started drug-discovery work of its own. It said it acquired Mithril Medicine, whose founder, Cody Tranbarger, used Claude to organize contracts, logistics, and experiments with 11 external labs, taking a possible muscular-dystrophy treatment from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months. Anthropic said that if those candidates continue to hold up, it expects a drug could be ready to start human trials as soon as late 2028, and that the work so far is mostly preclinical. It also said it has rolled out Claude Science, a workbench for researchers, and a Life Sciences Verification Program that lets trusted organizations use more permissive safeguards.

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1: Tom's Hardware says most of the first-half compute bill went to R&D, not serving Claude
items.summary: Anthropic said Oct. 26 that Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 for a proposed Nasdaq listing of Class A common stock under the symbol ANT, and that the share count and price range are not set. Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 29, citing that filing, that first-half 2026 compute and infrastructure spending was $8.95 billion, of which $2.38 billion was the cost of serving customers, against $16.29 billion in revenue. Tom's Hardware said the filing describes a multi-chip architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs, including about $161.2 billion in Broadcom TPU equipment-lease rent and at least $114.5 billion with Google. Tom's Hardware's own sum of the named deals is about $782 billion to $807 billion, and it said the S-1 leaves its own total blank.

items.headline: OpenAI reorganizes the Model Spec around five values, including human intent and care
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 29 it updated the Model Spec, its public description of how it wants models to behave, and reorganized the guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. OpenAI said the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance. It said OpenAI writes the Spec and sets boundaries, developers direct applications within those boundaries, and users direct the model's work subject to those constraints. OpenAI said the Spec describes behavior it is working toward and that its models do not yet fully reflect it.

items.headline: OpenAI and ServiceNow will connect ServiceNow workflows to ChatGPT and Codex
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 28 it is expanding its partnership with ServiceNow so ServiceNow products use more OpenAI models and agents, and so ServiceNow workflows connect to ChatGPT and Codex. OpenAI said a ServiceNow integration will let an IT team member find similar incidents, assess the risk of a change, and update a ServiceNow record inside ChatGPT, with ServiceNow's Action Fabric applying the customer's existing rules and permissions. The ServiceNow MCP plugin is available in the OpenAI marketplace now. OpenAI said voice features in the Super Intelligence Control Tower are expected in the first quarter of 2027, security capabilities are expected in early access in January 2027 and generally available in the second quarter of 2027, and Codex in the AI Workflow Factory is expected in 2027.

items.headline: OpenAI and Oracle will put Oracle applications and data into ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 27 it is expanding its partnership with Oracle so Oracle applications and data come into ChatGPT, and so new Oracle products use OpenAI models. Oracle is developing Oracle AI Workspace for that, and OpenAI said Oracle also announced Oracle AI Security Mesh, an SMB bundle that combines ChatGPT Business and Codex with Oracle applications and cloud credits, and Oracle App Composer for building apps with Codex. OpenAI said U.S. Oracle customers can buy the OpenAI API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work through Oracle Marketplace with eligible Universal Credits. OpenAI said Oracle reported 130,000 active ChatGPT users and more than 95,000 active Codex users.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, priced at half of GPT-5.6 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI said it is releasing GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster model for visual reasoning, computer use and writing, and that standard API prices are 50 percent lower than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. The prices it lists are $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens. OpenAI says that at medium reasoning effort on Agents' Last Exam, Terra scores 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra at about one-third the cost, matches GPT-6 Astra at one-tenth the price per token, and finishes tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra. OpenAI says Terra meets the Critical cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework and keeps the safeguards built for GPT-6 Astra.

items.headline: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, opening it first to cyber defenders
items.summary: Google said Oct. 28 that Gemini 4 Carbon is its strongest model for cybersecurity and long-horizon work, and that it ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 at 59. Google said Carbon scores 88.2 percent on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8 percent on ExploitGym, and 71.0 percent on CWE-bench, and that introductory pricing matches Gemini 4 Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google said it is in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release testing process, and that starting this week Carbon goes to a subset of cyber defenders and then to more trusted partners through the Fairwind Program before a wider release. Google said that after the introductory period the price becomes $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.

items.headline: Google announces Genie 4, a world model with native audio and real-time scene control
items.summary: Google said Oct. 27 it is announcing research on Genie 4, a world model for real-time interactive simulation with native audio. Google said Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, and that other Gemini models help keep a simulation coherent. A person can steer a scene in real time with natural language, including moving the camera, changing the weather, or adding characters, and the model generates ambient sound, music, and dialogue as the scene runs. Google said it has started a rollout to a limited group of trusted testers, and that Genie 4 is coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and to early-access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio.

items.headline: Google Cloud makes an Anthropic-managed Claude deployment generally available
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 23 that an Anthropic-managed option for Claude models on Google Cloud is generally available, alongside the existing Google-managed option. Google says both deliver the same frontier models on day zero, the same pricing, and Google Cloud billing, including drawdown of eligible commitments. On the Anthropic-managed option, Anthropic is the data processor under its own terms, and Claude platform features such as Managed Agents in beta, skills, and code execution are available on day zero. Google names Claude Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 5.5, and says customers authenticate with Google Cloud IAM.

items.headline: NVIDIA and Meta expand work on Muse, and NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 26 that it and Meta will expand their partnership on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training. NVIDIA said the companies will also consider further work on the OpenShell reference architecture and on Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. Meta intends to expand deployment of Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs, and NVIDIA said Meta will deploy Spectrum-X Ethernet and BlueField-4. NVIDIA said it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. Jensen Huang said the partnership is meant to optimize infrastructure for agents, and Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is how Meta brings what he called personal superintelligence to everyone.

items.headline: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight speech model for 40 languages
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 28 that Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight speech model for transcription, speaker labels, translation, and questions about a recording, in 40 languages including seven Indic languages. NVIDIA said it ranks first on the Hugging Face Open ASR leaderboard and second among open-weight models on Artificial Analysis, with about 4.3 billion active parameters, which NVIDIA said is 80 percent fewer than the leading open-weight model. NVIDIA said the weights are on Hugging Face today. It said quantized versions are coming so the model can run locally on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, and Jetson AGX Thor, or scale up on Blackwell data-center GPUs.

items.headline: OpenAI signs an AI-safety research agreement with Poland's NASK institute
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 23 it signed an agreement with Poland's NASK National Research Institute to collaborate on AI safety, security, and technical research. NASK's AI Safety Research Center will act as the Polish Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute. OpenAI said the work will cover evaluating capable systems, finding vulnerabilities, and strengthening safeguards. It also said CERT Polska, which operates within NASK, used Daybreak models in July to help find six vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS, including flaws that could be combined to take control of devices without authentication, and that the vendor's fixes blocked the attacks CERT Polska had seen.
